_meta.robot: humanoid_lite, legs only, 12 joints, 2 CAN buses
_meta.purpose: machine-readable input for humanoid-policy; every value derived from the capture JSONs in docs/measurements/, not hand-entered
_meta.READ_FIRST: CORRECTION 2026-09-29: the 09-28 'measC walk' ran the August policies/walk bundle, NOT measC-full (verified by replaying the tick log through every ONNX). measC-full has never been walked on hardware. Every *measC* WALK number below (circle, shuffle, knee swing, hip_yaw drift, ankle saturation, gait frequency, knee corr) belongs to that August bundle. measC's STAND numbers are verified. SPLIT VERDICT 2026-09-28. measC has the BEST STAND ever measured (tilt rate 0.04 deg/s untouched, 10x smoothA) and a WORSE WALK than smoothA: it shuffles (knee swing 0.17-0.24 rad vs sim 0.849) and walks in a CIRCLE (both hip_yaw drift 14-22 deg over 12 s against a zero yaw command, never recovering). The two objectives may be in tension -- a policy trained to hold position very tightly may be learning not to move. Also: the knee torque penalty MOVED load to the ankles rather than removing it (left_ankle_pitch now 3.9x its cap and above the motor ceiling). See REPORT_2026-09-28_measC_walk.md. M7 RESULT 2026-09-28: the joints are NOT soft -- every leg servo delivers kp=45 (medians 44.8-45.2 on all 10 joints), Kt*gear and URDF masses verified against gravity. Do NOT lower kp or rescale effort limits in sim. The reconstructed hardware torque (kp*err) equals ESC-commanded torque, so the 3-5x saturation gap is real demand; its cause is dynamic (filter/armature/damping) and not yet measured. See REPORT_2026-09-28_M7.md. A/B 2026-09-29 (same calibration, back to back): measD and measC-full are indistinguishable standers untouched (tilt rate 0.06 vs 0.04 deg/s, both at the IMU floor) and on push recovery; measD is worse on the stand-up ramp (5 vs 1 excursions >8 deg), matching sim's ranking. measD stands ~11 deg straighter-kneed with ~15% less holding torque. Use measC-full for the next hardware tests. See REPORT_2026-09-29_AB_measD_vs_measC.md.

joint_pos_noise.guidance: do NOT set the training value to the floor alone — measA did that and regressed. Split into sensor floor + calibration offset + an explicit unmodelled-plant margin.

joint_vel_noise.method: median of per-0.2s-window std; filtered signal (velocity_filter_alpha 0.7154)

observation_delay.model_as: single uniform delay tau ~ U(0, 10ms), ALL joints

stale_hold.guidance: DO NOT MODEL. 0.00% stale-hold across all captures despite real transport-layer frame loss; a 25 Hz consumer of a 100 Hz feed always has a fresh frame.

per_joint_delay_stagger.guidance: DO NOT MODEL. Cross-joint age spread is 0.17-1.11 ms against a 10 ms frame period. No poll-slot structure on this 2-bus robot; Asimov's per-CAN-slot model does not transfer.

base_ang_vel_noise.status: NOT MEASURED — gyro auto-zeroes at rest, so the floor is not observable standing still. Route around it via the high-frequency residual during a walk capture.

gyro_bias.guidance: DO NOT MODEL. Leave NoiseModelWithAdditiveBiasCfg off base_ang_vel rather than populate it with a guess.

calibration_offset.applies_to: per-episode START only — the offset is fixed once calibrated and does not change during a run. Model as add_all_joint_default_pos resampled at reset, constant within the episode.
calibration_offset.guidance: hip_roll and hip_yaw are DECLARED zero by the operator's stance rather than resting on a hardstop, and are correspondingly less repeatable. The left leg is ~2x less repeatable than the right. Per-joint half-widths are available above if uniform randomisation proves too blunt.
calibration_offset.not_covered: this does NOT measure encoder drift WITHIN a run. That is a separate error source with a different sim model (slowly-varying bias, not a per-reset constant) and is still unmeasured.

sample_age_ms.model_as: single uniform delay tau ~ U(0, 10ms), ALL joints

torque_caps_nm.status: flashed and verified by SDO readback 2026-09-25

knee_torque_saturation.status: measured on hardware (RECONSTRUCTED as kp*err - kd*vel, not measured torque); M7 is required to break the circularity | M7 2026-09-28: ESC torque == kp*err statically, so the reconstruction IS the ESC's commanded torque, not a circular artifact.
knee_torque_saturation.guidance: a ~4x sim/hardware gap at one joint is a PLANT modelling error. No reward shaping closes it; in sim the knees barely saturate, so a knee-overshoot penalty has nothing to act on and hits the ankles.
knee_torque_saturation.CORRECTION_2026-09-29: hardware_fraction_measC: CORRECTION_2026-09-29: from the 09-28 walk, which ran the August policies/walk bundle, not measC-full

joint_velocity_limit.status: HARD HARDWARE CONSTRAINT until the ESC is upgraded
joint_velocity_limit.guidance: the ESC cannot track the encoder above ~13 rad/s at the joint; it raises ERROR_ENCODER_FAULT (0x2000) and floods EMCY until the bus drops. smoothA never exceeded 1.08 rad/s standing.
joint_velocity_limit.CORRECTION_2026-09-28: the earlier 2.0 figure was smoothA's STANDING max and was wrong for a limit that binds during walking. smoothA's walk capture gives a median per-joint max of 6.90 rad/s with peaks 7.1-8.8; a hinge at 2.0 priced its normal gait and measB-fast came out a shuffle (knee corr -0.158 vs -0.655). Use 8.0.
joint_velocity_limit.NOT_THE_FAULT_TRIGGER_2026-09-28: the 2026-09-28 fault came at 5.84 rad/s while two ankles survived 8.8-9.8 rad/s in the same disturbance, and the left knee survived MORE implied torque than the right. Velocity does not explain node 8. Keep the 8.0 hinge as general safety (smoothA peaks 14.98 in sim) but it will not prevent this fault.

ankle_torque_saturation.guidance: THE NEW BOTTLENECK. left_ankle_pitch demands 3.9x its cap and ABOVE the MAD5010 physical ceiling. The knee torque reward moved load off the knees (52.1% -> 25.1%) and onto the ankles. Make the torque term GLOBAL over all joints normalised by each cap, or it just redistributes. Prefer reducing demand over raising the cap -- the ankle is 3D-printed and has already broken mechanically.
ankle_torque_saturation.CORRECTION_2026-09-29: CORRECTION_2026-09-29: from the 09-28 walk, which ran the August policies/walk bundle, not measC-full

m7_static_stiffness.status: MEASURED 2026-09-28, legs hanging, all 12 held, limb weight as load
m7_static_stiffness.verdict: stiffness hypothesis REFUTED: servo kp == commanded 45 on every leg joint
m7_static_stiffness.kt_gear_and_urdf_mass_verified: ESC torque / URDF gravity torque 0.94-1.07 on hips and right knee

static_friction_nm.note: median torque beyond gravity at settle; per-point scatter +-0.5 N·m on hips = stiction

m7_static_stiffness.left_knee_anomaly: extra torque +0.2 -> +0.9 N·m growing with angle, left only (cable/rub/unmodelled mass); right knee ~0
m7_static_stiffness.do_not_use: m7_sweep's gravity-slope kp_eff, L/R ratios, direction asymmetry and frame columns -- friction-dominated fits
m7_static_stiffness.guidance: do NOT lower kp or rescale effort limits to model softness. Add ankle_pitch static friction ~0.4 N·m. The sim/hardware torque gap is dynamic and not yet measured: firmware torque filter (alpha 0.1454, ~50 Hz), armature, damping. Feet collide when both hip_yaw turn the same world direction beyond ~34-38 deg.

yaw_drift_during_gait_rad.guidance: NEW FAILURE MODE. Both hip_yaw joints drift monotonically 14-22 deg over 12 s and never return, in the same world-frame direction, against a ZERO yaw-rate command. The robot walks in a circle. Nothing in the reward prices yaw drift against a zero yaw command -- add a heading/yaw-tracking term.

standing_constraint.guidance: every gait figure in these reports describes a SUPPORTED walk, with the operator's hand on the robot. Hardware fall rates are therefore not comparable to sim fall_rate/min. Standing unattended is the nearer milestone: smoothA clears it, smoothB clears it until pushed, measA does not.
